Compressor 6.1 General 6.1.1 Compressor, prime mover and auxiliary equipment shall be designed the specified operating conditions and for rapid and easy maintenance, packing and valves. 6.1.2 Where special area classification followed for the design and construction i.2 Cylinder 6.2.1 Maximum allowable working pressure shall exceed rated discharge pressure by at least 10 percent or 1 bar whichever is greater but must not be lower than safety valve set pressure. 6.2.2 Cylinders without liners and having bore of 150 mm and above shall have wall of sufficient :hickness to provide for a total of I.5 mm in diameter for reboring without affecting the maximum 3jlowable working pressure or maximum allowable rod loading. 6.2.3 Cylinders shall be spaced and arranged to permit access to all openings, 3nd controls without removing the cylinder, cylinder head or major piping. 6.2.4 Cylinders shall have adequate cooling provision. not be less valves, packings for the required duty at particularly regarding

9. Vibration and Critical SpeedsIn case the entire system is supplied by the compressor manufacturer or supplier shall assume full responsibility for the performance of necessary torsional studies and the elimination of any lateral or torsional vibrations that may hinder the operation of the complete unit within the specified operating range in any specified loading step, The manufacturer shall state the speeds ( from dead stop up to or down from trip speed or synchronous speed ) at which all critical speeds occur. If a gear reducer is provided, the design of the compressor driver train shall prevent any torsion from exceeding the limits allowed by any major component ( compressor, prime mover, gear coupling, or the like) of the train. Torsional natural frequencies of the prime mover compressor system ( including couplings and any gear unit) should be avoided within 10 percent of any shaft speeds and within 5 percent of twice any shaft speed in the rotating system. NoteIO. This requirement is essential for compressors above 150 kW.

10.2.3 Safety Valves - Each stage shall be protected by a safety valve. This safety valve shall be dimensioned for full compressor capacity with set pressure not more than maximum allowable *working pressure for that stage. The safety valves shall not disturbed by the vibration. be as designed and mounted in such a manner that the setting is

No additional safety valve after the final stage is required if a safety valve of proper size is provided on the air receiver and there is no stop valve from discharge of the final stage and the air receiver.

Guarantees shall be guaranteed for satisfactory performance 14.1 Performance Guarantee - The compressor at the specified operating conditions. These include a guarantee for flow rate and power at the time of performance test unless guarantees on other items have been specifically asked by the purchaser. This guarantee shall be applicable for a period of 12 months or 2000 h from the date of installation whichever is earlier, If any defects or malperformance is established during the guarantee period the supplier shall make all necessary or desirable alterations, repairs and replacements free of charge. EXPLANATORY

NOTE

With the consistently increasing use of compressors in diversified fields, need was felt to bring out standards on performance and other data, useful to both users and manufacturers. Considerable progress has been made in this direction during last few years by the publication of some standards relating to compressors. This standard covers the technical supply condition for reciprocating air compressors above supply conditions for reciprocating air compressors for above 25 kW up to and 60 kW. Technical Technical supply conditions for including 60 kW are covered in separate standard IS : 11012-1984. rec~`procatiilg com~p~ressors t$el'ciw~P??ti?O:are &e~!ng covered' serjara&t). 13
